changelog: The campaign has an ending, and every general has three ways to play. Twenty-six versions landed since the last Mac build. Act IV: the Abaddon finale The campaign now ends. Act IV adds the Abaddon finale and two new commanders on the way — the Tormentor and the Charioteer, each with their own portrait and dialogue. The finale boss is not a bigger version of an earlier one: it runs every mechanic it absorbed over the run, so the fight is a reckoning with the acts you just played. Three ways to play every general Each general now has archetypes — distinct builds rather than one optimal line — and picking one weights your drafting toward it, so a run commits to a plan instead of drifting toward whatever the shop offered. Doctrine is the new card type that carries them, and doctrines stack. Old Guard and Caravan are filled out first: Hold Fast, Mentor, Unbroken, Wagon Train, Supply Run and Rolling Depot. Every unit’s numbers changed A full rebalance: new stat lines, a reworked rank-up rule, and per-ally flanking rather than a flat bonus. Ion Cannon pierces. The Bannerman’s aura is visible when you select it, reaches one tile, and two at rank 5. Upgrades the rebalance had quietly turned into no-ops were reworked rather than left in, the AI plays the new rules, and Drones fly. Deployment is a real decision Your army starts in reserve. A roster panel opens after the reveal and you place units yourself, or hit Auto Deploy and let it fill the HQ’s rings from the inside out. Deployment is a hard gate, the opening hand is dealt when you commit, and the draw and discard piles are actual cards that animate. Skirmishes fight differently Skirmish enemies act from a per-type table instead of a CP-and-era deck, so they read as units rather than as a budget. The reinforcement bar grows by act and by step, and Holdout and Survive have no reinforcement cap at all. Card art is complete 174 of 174 cards now have their own art. The card base also got an audit pass: duplicates removed, strictly-worse pairs fixed, price outliers brought into line. Rulings, tightened A played card reaches its pile only after it resolves. An unplayed One-Shot goes to the discard at end of turn. Emplacement is ground-only. Boss spoils lean out, and commanders that never leave home no longer turn up in Survive or Hold. Interface The plate system is finished — the last buttons carrying baked-in English now draw their own labels, which is what makes a translated build possible. Values sit in their bronze wells with gold glyph digits, the header plaque behaves on narrow frames, phone layouts fit one row, and the run summary lives at the top of Settings instead of its own screen. Mac Universal (Apple Silicon and Intel), Developer ID signed, notarized and stapled. Minimum macOS 11. 1,241 tests.
